name: Probe enclosure
purpose: A deliberate grip for low-contact-force imaging, with two controls and a visible status strip.
interface: Illustrative envelope: 150 × 56 × 34 mm. Tether routes to a separate acquisition unit.
test: Gloved reach, cleaning, balance and contact-force usability studies.

name: Ultrasound cartridge
purpose: The primary structural imaging channel. Begin with a conventional linear-array module.
interface: Candidate 7–15 MHz band; acoustic coupling, receive chain and synchronized acquisition.
test: Point-spread function, vessel localization, near-field performance and deformation.

name: Photoacoustic rails
purpose: Experimental hemoglobin contrast, registered with ultrasound rather than used as an autonomous diagnosis.
interface: Tethered laboratory source first. Evaluate 850 nm LEDs and a 1064 nm pulsed-source alternative.
test: Incremental benefit over US alone, exposure, heating, pigmentation effects and motion.

name: Passive contact shoe
purpose: Replaceable interface with an open working corridor and proposed contact-force sensing.
interface: Acoustic and optical transmission; no active suction in the initial design.
test: Transmission loss, air gaps, vessel compression, cleaning and sterility requirements.

name: Acquisition & monitoring
purpose: Coordinate acquisition and monitor contact and temperature, with a proposed independent optical interlock.
interface: Separate bench source/acquisition unit; the complete system is not contained in this handle.
test: Synchronization, registration, failure states, latency, power and thermal budgets.
